title: Pauri 5, sound: thaapiaa na jaae
hook: thaapiaa na jaae keetaa na hoe

segments.voice: Yesterday, nadar, the gracious glance that opens the door. Your line was the early hour opens.

People make things and set them in place all the time: a trophy in a cabinet, a photo on a shelf, a sign over a shop door. Made, put in place, and there they stay. Today a new stretch of Japji begins, pauris five to eight, and the fifth pauri opens by saying, twice, that the One can't be handled that way. It says it in a line built from two short no's, with a soft, rolling sound.
screen: `A TROPHY SET IN PLACE.` → `A NEW STRETCH: PAURIS 5 TO 8.` → `TWO SHORT NO'S.`

segments.voice: The opening line: thaapiaa na jaae, keetaa na hoe. Thaapiaa: THAA-pi-aa. The th isn't the English th in thin; it's a t with a puff of breath after it, like the t in top said firmly. Thaap means to set up, to install, to establish, the way an image is set on a pedestal. Na jaae: na, not; JAA-ay, can be. Keetaa: KEE-taa, made. Na hoe: na, not; HO-ay, is, becomes. Cannot be installed, cannot be made: two no's, balanced on either side of the line like the two pans of a scale. Then the next line: aape aap niranjan soe. AA-pay aap: himself, by himself. Ni-RUN-jun: stainless, unstained. He is Himself, by Himself, the stainless one. Hear the rhythm: short phrases, each ending on a soft vowel, jaae, hoe, soe. It rocks gently, back and forth. Later in this pauri comes a refrain you'll hear again in the next one: guraa ik dehi bujhaaee. Guraa: Guru. Ik: one. Dehi bujhaaee: give understanding. It's read two ways: as a request, O Guru, give me this one understanding, or as thanks, the Guru has given this one understanding. What that understanding is, tomorrow. So the pauri starts with two no's about what the One is not, and ends with a yes: one understanding, given by the Guru.
screen: `THAAP — TO SET UP, TO INSTALL.` · `TWO NO'S, LIKE A SCALE.` · `AAPE AAP NIRANJAN SOE.` · `GURAA IK DEHI BUJHAAEE.` · then, large: `PAURI FIVE.`

segments.voice: Say it slowly, out loud if you can, with a light puff of breath on the th: thaapiaa na jaae, keetaa na hoe. Add the next line, aape aap niranjan soe, and say all of it once more, softly, feeling it rock back and forth. Then sit in the quiet; if you pray, you can rest in Waheguru.
screen: `ਥਾਪਿਆ ਨ ਜਾਇ ਕੀਤਾ ਨ ਹੋਇ ॥ ਆਪੇ ਆਪਿ ਨਿਰੰਜਨੁ ਸੋਇ ॥`

segments.voice: Niranjan. Stainless, unstained: the One who cannot be installed or made, thaapiaa na jaae, keetaa na hoe.
Your line: thaapiaa na jaae. The One can't be set in place, or made. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: The fifth pauri of Japji is recited each morning; its refrain, guraa ik dehi bujhaaee, about the one understanding the Guru gives, comes back at the end of the sixth pauri.

trapdoor: what you thought: a line about something that can't be done.
what it means: the One cannot be installed or made; He is Himself, by Himself, stainless.
what a scholar hears: thaapiaa uses the verb for installing an image on its seat; niranjan is from anjan, the black of collyrium: without a stain.

notes: Thaap as installing an image: common gloss. Confirm framing avoids disparaging image worship (the script only says 'the One can't be handled that way').
Niranjan from anjan (collyrium): common etymology. Confirm.
Refrain 'guraa ik dehi bujhaaee' in pauris 5 and 6: confirm.
